subject: environmental
audience: FE Environmental candidates and environmental engineering students
title: The Incinerator That Achieved 99.9%, Not 99%
featured_title: THE INCINERATOR THAT ACHIEVED 99.9 PERCENT, NOT 99

presentation.challenge: An outlet of 0.025 kg/hr from a 25 kg/hr hazardous constituent feed means only 0.1% remains. The destruction/removal efficiency is 99.9%.

practice.primary_question: How is destruction and removal efficiency calculated from hazardous constituent feed and outlet mass rates?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Confusing the outlet fraction with the percent remaining or losing a decimal place when converting a small mass-rate ratio to percent.

case_dna.target_misconception: An outlet-to-inlet ratio of 0.001 means 1% remains and therefore only 99% is removed.
case_dna.why_plausible: Decimal fractions and percentages differ by a factor of 100, so 0.001 is easily misread as 1%.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: 0.025/25=0.001 as a fraction, which is 0.1%. Therefore DRE=(1-0.001)×100=99.9%.
case_dna.corrected_model: Compute the outlet-to-inlet mass-rate fraction first, convert it correctly to percent, and subtract from 100% to obtain destruction/removal efficiency.

problem_statement: A hazardous-waste thermal treatment unit receives 25 kg/hr of a target organic constituent. The measured constituent mass rate in the treated exhaust is 0.025 kg/hr. Using DRE=[(Win-Wout)/Win]×100%, a note reports 99% because it treats 0.001 as 1%. Determine the correct DRE.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The mass ratio was right. The percentage conversion was not.
gates.prompt: What percentage does a fraction of 0.001 represent?

options.label: Use DRE=[1-(Wout/Win)]×100%
options.reason: This is algebraically equivalent to the stated DRE definition.

options.label: Use DRE=(Wout/Win)×100%
options.reason: That gives percent remaining, not percent destroyed or removed.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the DRE
gates.success: The outlet is 0.1% of the inlet, so DRE=99.9%.
gates.hint: Multiply a decimal fraction by 100 to express it as percent.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: The small outlet mass corresponds to 0.1% remaining

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the treatment-efficiency note
report: C1. Inlet constituent rate is 25 kg/hr.
C2. Outlet constituent rate is 0.025 kg/hr.
C3. Since 0.025/25=0.001, 1% remains and DRE is 99%.

claims.label: C1
claims.reason: This is the stated inlet mass rate.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: This is the stated outlet mass rate.

evidence_choices.label: 0.001×100%=0.1%, so DRE=99.9%
evidence_choices.reason: This is the correct fraction-to-percent conversion.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Reach 99.99% DRE at the same inlet rate

options.label: Limit Wout to 0.0025 kg/hr or less

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply DRE to another treatment unit
gates.prompt: A unit receives 10 kg/hr and releases 0.05 kg/hr of the target constituent. What is DRE?

options.reason: That is the percentage remaining, not the DRE.

gates.explanation: DRE is the fraction removed from the inlet mass rate, expressed as a percentage.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the hazardous-waste treatment calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that destruction/removal efficiency is based on inlet and outlet constituent mass rates and requires careful fraction-to-percent conversion.

items.label: What failed
items.value: A decimal fraction was converted to percent incorrectly.

seo.meta_description: Solve FE Environmental Case E-079: reducing a hazardous constituent from 25 kg/hr to 0.025 kg/hr gives 99.9% destruction/removal efficiency.
seo.excerpt: A tiny outlet-to-inlet ratio can be easy to misread. Convert the fraction to percent carefully before reporting treatment efficiency.
seo.direct_answer: Wout/Win=0.025/25=0.001, which is 0.1% remaining. Therefore DRE=[1-0.001]×100=99.9%.
